<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par72 />{{GHGmargin-letter|72|f}}
'''4.''' The cases of unusual vowel lengthening mentioned in ''b'' are: {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=יָקוּם}} (also in Arabic ''yăqûmu''), but {{GHGterm|jussive}} with normal lengthening ({{GHGpar|48|g}}), {{GHGheb|text=יָקֹם}}, with retraction of the tone {{GHGheb|text=יָ֫קָם}} (''yāqŏm''), {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫קָם}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫קֹם}}); {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}}, with normal lengthening of the ''ŭ'' in the 2nd ''plur. fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=קֹ֫מְנָה}}, since, according to {{GHGpar|26|p}}, the ''û'' cannot be retained in a closed penultima; {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}}. In {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} the original ''ĭ'' is naturally lengthened to ''î'' ({{GHGheb|text=הֵקִים}}, {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יָקִים}}, {{GHGterm|jussive}} {{GHGheb|text=יָקִם}}, with retraction of the tone {{GHGheb|text=יָ֫קֶם}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫קֶם}}); on the transference of this ''î'' to the {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} of the strong verb, cf. {{GHGpar|53|a}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|g}}
The following forms require special consideration: the {{GHGterm|participle Qal}} {{GHGheb|text=קָם}} is to be traced to the ground-form with ''â'' unobscured, Arab. ''qâtĭl'', {{GHGpar|9|q}}, and {{GHGpar|50|b}}. On this analogy the form would be ''qâĭm'',<ref>So in Arabic, prop. ''qâʾĭm'', since the two vowels are kept apart by the insertion of an {{GHGheb|text=א}}, cf. Aram. {{GHGheb|text=קָאֵם}}; but also contracted, as ''šâk'', ''hâr'', for ''šâʾĭk'', &c. (cf. Wright’s ''Gramm. of the Arabic Language'', 2nd ed. vol. i. p. 164).</ref> which after absorption of the ''ĭ'' became {{GHGheb|text=קָם}}, owing to the predominating character of the ''â''. The unchangeableness of the ''â'' (''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=קָמִים}}, {{GHGterm|constr.}} {{GHGheb|text=קָמֵי}}, &c.) favours this explanation.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|h}}
In the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}, besides the forms with original ''ŭ'' (now ''û'') there are also forms with original ''ă''. This ''ă'' was lengthened to ''ā'', and then further obscured to ''ô''; hence especially {{GHGheb|text=(יָבֹא) יָבוֹא}}, {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּבֹא}}, &c., from the {{GHGterm|perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=בָּא|translate=he has come}}. In the ''imperfects'' {{GHGheb|text=יֵאוֹר}} (but cf. {{GHGheb|text=וַתָּאֹ֫רְנָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=27}}) and {{GHGheb|text=יֵבוֹשׁ}} from the ''intransitive perfects'' {{GHGheb|text=אוֹר}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּשׁ}} (see above, c), most probably also in {{GHGheb|text=יֵאֹ֫תוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=12|verse=9}}, {{GHGheb|text=נֵאוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=15}} from an unused {{GHGheb|text=אות|translate=to consent}}, and perhaps in {{GHGheb|text=וַתֵּהֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=5}}, &c., as in the cases noticed in {{GHGpar|63|e}} and especially {{GHGpar|67|n}}, the ''ē'' of the preformative is lengthened from ''ĭ'' (which is attenuated from original ''ă'') and thus ''yĭ-băš'' became ''yĭ-bāš'', and finally ''yē-bôš''. Finally the ''Niph.'' {{GHGheb|text=נָקוֹם}} (''nă-qām''), {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יִקּוֹם}} from ''yiqqām'', originally ({{GHGpar|51|m}}) ''yinqăm'', arises in the same way from the obscuring of ''ā'' lengthened from ''ă''.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|i}}
'''5.''' In the {{GHGterm|perfect Niphʿal}} and {{GHGterm|Hiphʿîl}} a {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}} is inserted before the afformatives beginning with a consonant in the 1st and 2nd persons, and {{GHGheb|text=־ֶי}} regularly (but see Rem.) in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Qal}}, sometimes also in the {{GHGterm|imperfect Hiphʿîl}} (as in {{GHGheb|text=תְּבִיאֶ֫ינָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=7|verse=30}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=תְּהִימֶ֫נָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=12}}), before the termination of {{GHGheb|text=נָה}}. As in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}} ({{GHGpar|67|d}} and note) these ''separating vowels'' serve as an artificial opening of the preceding syllable, in order to preserve the long vowel; in the {{GHGterm|perfect Hiphʿîl}}, however, before the {{GHGheb|text=וֹ}}, instead of the ''î'' an ''ē'' is somewhat often found<ref>{{GHGheb|text=וַֽהֲשֵֽׁיבֹתֶם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=6|verse=7}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=6|verse=25}}) could only be an orthographic licence for {{GHGheb|text=והשֵֽׁב׳}}; perhaps, however, {{GHGheb|text=והשִֽׁיב׳}} was originally intended.</ref> (as a normal lengthening of the original ''ĭ''), especially after ''wāw {{hyphenated word start|con|consecutive}}''<section end=par72 /><noinclude>
